'''Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)''' was an unofficial GeoCities SWCCG fan site for the Corellia region, hosted at <code>geocities.com/plarathas/</code> and <code>geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/</code>. It carried decks, strategy, card reviews, a player database, [[Anagrams|Anagramed Decipherians]], and the [[Squadron Members]] roster, and was not produced or endorsed by Decipher or Lucasfilm.<ref name="home2005">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/index-2.html Corellian Engineering homepage] (geocities.ws mirror). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010055453/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/index-2.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The webmaster wrote from an Indiana State University address and used the GeoCities name <code>plarathas</code>. A sidebar ranked the site in a Top 100 CCG list as id <code>gold31</code>. The last homepage update, dated 15 August 2005 (GenCon / SWCCG Worlds in Indianapolis), said the site had reopened and was looking for contributors.<ref name="home2005" />

Nav-bar "Top SWCCG Sites" on the 2005 homepage: Decipher Inc, Corellian Engineering, SWCCG Players Committee, [[DeckTech]], [[GamePlayers Network]], HoloTable, SWCCG Database.<ref name="home2005" />


== Deck designs ==

The Deck Designs page listed Classic Star Wars Light and Dark plus Young Jedi Jedi and Sith. Every capture from 9 July 2000 through 23 October 2009 shows the same index titles and an empty Classic Dark heading.<ref name="decks2000">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000709072031/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/decks.html decks.html] (Wayback, 9 July 2000).</ref><ref name="decksws">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks.html Deck Designs] (geocities.ws mirror). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261013084053/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/decks.html Internet Archive]</ref> Wayback kept light1.html, light2.html, and jedi1.html from the CollegePark host (December 2001). light3.html and sith1.html were not captured on the original GeoCities host; they survive on the geocities.ws mirror.

The Classic Star Wars reading copies are on [[Corellian Engineering Corporation decks]]. Young Jedi lists stay on the archived HTML.

== Mirrors and archives ==

* Original GeoCities home (Wayback, HTTP 200): [https://web.archive.org/web/20010513005725/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/ 13 May 2001] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20010517194935/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/ 17 May 2001] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20010526161604/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/ 26 May 2001] · [https://web.archive.org/web/20010721002349/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/ 21 July 2001]
* Original <code>geocities.com/plarathas/SMs.html</code> on Wayback is [https://web.archive.org/web/20091028130457/http://geocities.com/plarathas/SMs.html 28 October 2009, HTTP 410] (after Yahoo closed GeoCities).
* [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/ geocities.ws/plarathas] (live third-party mirror) (Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008210620/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/ Internet Archive])
* [https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/ oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433] (live; Wayback from 2019, including [https://web.archive.org/web/20190131115529/http://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html anagrams.html 31 January 2019])
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20160406045459/http://www.reocities.com/CollegePark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html reocities anagrams] (Wayback 6 April 2016; also 9 May 2014 and 20 February 2016) — the URL Encyclopedia 3.2 cites<ref name="enc32" />

The 13 May 2001 original home has more than the 2005 mirror.<ref name="home2001">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010513005725/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/ Original GeoCities home] (Wayback, 13 May 2001).</ref> It says Decipher's site mentioned CEC twice ([https://web.archive.org/web/20010513005725/http://www.decipher.com/newsflash/1999/0899/080499storyB.html 4 August 1999] and [https://web.archive.org/web/20010513005725/http://www.decipher.com/newsflash/1999/0999/092799storyA.html 27 September 1999]). It links sister site The Outpost (<code>tco.htmlplanet.com</code>) and hosts Jeff Hansen's ([[Jeff Hansen|Rogue 5]]) "Neglected Cards". It advertises the 3rd Annual King of Corellia (Carmel, Indiana), a tournament [[John Sarnecki]] had introduced before retiring. Its TDs were [[Alex Alcalde]] Gold 31, [[John Kaufeld]], and [[Craig Spaid]] Bravo 36.<ref name="home2001" /> Other linked pages on that capture: Indiana.html, awards.html, pics.html, anagrams.html, ratings.html, stats.html, [http://kingofcorellia.homestead.com/ kingofcorellia.homestead.com], Star Wars CCG XChange (<code>pagesz.net/~billyak/swxchange</code>), Bill Yak's Final Conflict (<code>billyak.com/fc/</code>).

Yahoo closed GeoCities in 2009. The roster and anagram table survive through the 2001 Wayback captures and the oocities, geocities.ws, and reocities mirrors.
